new_statements.quote: Bahasa Rawas memiliki nada, tekanan, dan panjang. Akan tetapi, ketiga unsur ini tidak digolongkan ke dalam fonem dalam karena mereka tidak fonemik atau tidak membedakan arti leksikal kata. Dalam ujaran yang lebih panjang daripada kata, misalnya, frase atau kalimat, nada, tekanan, serta panjang memang mempunyai kemampuan mengubah arti. Walaupun demikian, kemampuan seperti ini lebih erat hubungannya dengan lagu kalimat atau intonasi. Intonasi tidak dibicarakan dalam bab ini, tetapi merupakan bahan yang akan disinggung dalam Bab 5 yang membicarakan struktur sintaksis. Analisa data menunjukkan bahwa fonem suprasegmental yang ada dalam bahasa Rawas adalah jeda.
new_statements.translation: Rawas has pitch, stress and length. However, these three elements are not classed among the phonemes because they are not phonemic, i.e. they do not distinguish the lexical meaning of words. In utterances longer than a word, e.g. phrases or sentences, pitch, stress and length do have the capacity to change meaning; even so, this capacity is more closely tied to sentence melody or intonation. Intonation is not discussed in this chapter but will be touched on in Chapter 5, which deals with syntactic structure. Analysis of the data shows that the suprasegmental phoneme present in Rawas is juncture.
new_statements.citation: Saleh, Yuslizal, M. Lamsari & Abdul Madjid. 1984. Struktur bahasa Rawas. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa (Departemen Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan). xvii+260 pp.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress exists phonetically but is non-contrastive at word level and is not assigned a position; meaning-bearing prominence is a matter of phrase/sentence intonation. The only suprasegmental phoneme recognised is juncture (four kinds, §3.5.1 ff.). No word-stress placement rule is stated in the snippets recovered (the full page could not be opened).
new_statements.domain_note: Word ('kata') vs. longer utterances ('frase atau kalimat'): stress/pitch/length said to lack lexical contrast at word level and to matter only as intonation at phrase/sentence level. The statement is reconstructed from overlapping verbatim scanned snippets served by Google Books (snippet view); the book itself was not opened, so the exact page (77 vs 79) and any placement remark elsewhere in §3.5 remain unverified.
new_statements.identity_note: rawa1268 is a retired ISO code (rws), merged into Musi [mui] by ISO change request 2007-182 (effective 2008-01-14). Glottolog 5.x treats Rawas as dialect rawa1270 'Rawas Musi' under Upper Musi (uppe1480) of Musi (musi1241); McDowell & Anderbeck 2020 place Rawas (Rupit, Rawas Ulu, Rawas Tengah sites) in the UPPER MUSI cluster of the MUSI language, ~200,000 speakers in Musi Rawas / Musi Rawas Utara, South Sumatra. The quoted source (Saleh et al. 1984) describes 'bahasa Rawas' as a whole; its introduction (per a Google Books snippet) treats Rawas under Musi Rawas regency without singling out a subdialect. Any catalog entry should be filed under musi1241 / rawa1270, not under the retired code.
